findings.doc_quote: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, glob string, or callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/types/types.py:330 — "FalseySentinel | V | Condition[V | FalseySentinel] | ComparisonCondition[V | FalseySentinel] | None" (no glob member); src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:763-765 — `if not callable(condition): ... return coerce_to_literal_type(actual, condition) == condition`. Runtime probe on a real RawStateChangeEvent with new state "on": P.StateTo("o*")(event) -> False, P.StateTo("on")(event) -> True.
findings.explanation: A plain string in a ChangeType position is compared by exact equality, with no glob detection. Auto-globbing exists only in DomainMatches, EntityMatches and ServiceMatches (`_glob_or_literal`, predicates.py:227-229) and in ServiceDataWhere (predicates.py:700). The bus helpers pass changed_from/changed_to straight to StateFrom/StateTo/AttrFrom/AttrTo (bus.py:1757-1762), so a glob string there never matches as a glob. The union also includes None and the falsy sentinels.
findings.suggested_fix: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, or callable (value) -> bool. A plain string compares exactly; use C.Glob("pattern") for glob matching (only P.ServiceDataWhere auto-wraps glob strings).

findings.doc_quote: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, a glob string, or any callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:321-322 — `extracted = self.source(value); return compare_value(extracted, self.condition)`; predicates.py:763-765 — non-callable conditions use equality. Runtime probe: P.ValueIs(source=lambda v: v, condition="light.*")("light.kitchen") -> False.
findings.explanation: P.ValueIs does not detect globs. A string such as "light.*" is compared as an exact literal, so a user following this line gets a predicate that silently never matches.
findings.suggested_fix: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance (use C.Glob for glob patterns; a bare glob string compares literally), or any callable (value) -> bool.

findings.doc_quote: The context dict from the event payload.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/events/base.py:31-37 — `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class HassContext: id: str; parent_id: str | None; user_id: str | None`; src/hassette/events/hass/hass.py:221 — `"context": HassContext(**event["context"])`. Runtime probe: A.get_context(event) -> HassContext(id='1', parent_id=None, user_id=None).
findings.explanation: get_context returns a frozen, slotted HassContext dataclass, not a dict. Treating it as a dict, for example ctx["user_id"], raises TypeError; use attribute access. The Returns column on the same row (HassContext) is correct; only the description is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: The HassContext object (attributes id, parent_id, user_id) from the event payload.

findings.doc_quote: The full service_data dict, or MISSING_VALUE when absent.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/events/hass/hass.py:22 — `service_data: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)`. Runtime probe: create_event_from_hass on a call_service event with no service_data gives A.get_service_data(event) -> {}.
findings.explanation: On a CallServiceEvent, the only event type this table lists, absent service_data becomes an empty dict, so this accessor returns {} rather than MISSING_VALUE. MISSING_VALUE appears only if the accessor runs on an event with no such path. get_service_data_key still returns MISSING_VALUE for an absent key (line 147 is correct).
findings.suggested_fix: The full service_data dict; empty when the service call carried none. Returns MISSING_VALUE only on events with no service_data field.

summary: The page is highly accurate on signatures, defaults, operators, import paths, coercion rules and accessor tables; coercion and condition behavior was also confirmed by runtime probes. Two of the four findings are the same high-severity error: lines 9 and 28 say ChangeType and P.ValueIs accept glob strings, but only DomainMatches, EntityMatches, ServiceMatches and ServiceDataWhere treat them as globs. The other two are accessor descriptions: get_context returns a HassContext dataclass rather than a dict, and get_service_data returns {} rather than MISSING_VALUE when a CallServiceEvent has no service_data.
